top.title: Fertilizer subsidy may rise 15% to ₹2.5 trillion even as sales fall 8%
top.description: India’s fertilizer subsidy bill could rise 15% to ₹2.5 trillion in FY27, near its record high, as global prices climb despite weaker demand. Fertilizer sales fell 8% in April-October, while deficient monsoon rains are expected to reduce annual consumption to 65-67 million tonnes.

primary.title: Making time to just be
primary.description: What if doing nothing is actually good for you? In a world that celebrates packed calendars, long working hours and endless productivity, this episode of The Happiness Lab, The Art of Doing Nothing, makes a welcome case for taking it easy.Host Laurie Santos explores 'time famine' - that familiar feeling of never having enough hours in the day. Drawing on the work of two experts, she questions why we often value money more than time. Writer Tom Hodgkinson, author of How to Be Idle, makes a case for idling, daydreaming, napping and spending time with friends without constantly checking the clock. These aren't signs of laziness, he argues, but part of what makes life enjoyable. He also takes a swipe at the idea that working hard is always a virtue, especially when it leaves little time for creativity and relationships.Harvard professor Ashley Whillans brings the science to the discussion, explaining how feeling short of time can make us less happy and even less inclined to help others. Her research suggests that paying someone to do chores can be money well spent if it gives us back free time.Santos keeps the discussion grounded, recognising that escaping deadlines is easier said than done. The takeaway? Happiness may have less to do with doing more, and more to do with occasionally doing absolutely nothing.
